[spoiler=A goddamn festivity and party LET'S GOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOO][b] 12 de Janeiro 2025[/b]
Quando os 3 Guardiões, Balunji, Mardu e Ngayhl se encontram juntos em um assentamento, geralmente no Djamuturu(estação chuvosa), muitos pedem conselhos e revelações a eles, foi oque Tjarrampa, do clã Marrapinti foi perguntar para Nghayhl sobre um sonho, ele usava roupas grossas e marrons, ele enrolava o próprio cabelo  para se distrair enquanto ia até o gunya dos  Koolemany.
[i]Grande sábio, essa noite tive um sonho estranho. [/i]
Ele disse ao entrar e fazer uma reverência, Ngayhl então olhou para ele, seus olhos pareciam focados não apenas no visitante, mas em sua própria alma.
[i]Oque tu sonhastes.[/i]
Ele perguntou já começando a segurar a folha de eucalipto em seu pescoço.
[i]Sonhei com nuvens escuras, muito escuras, que ao invés de chuva caiam lanças de mel, no momento em que atingiram um lago seco, ele reviveu e se encheu de água e peixes dourados saltaram de lá[/i].
O sábio sorriu, e então relaxou seu aperto no totem, e disse para Tjarrampa.
[i]Isso é sinal de um banquete próspero e de chuvas.[/i]
 [i]Abundância? excelente, agradeço.[/i]
Tjarrampa sorriu em resposta e então saiu do Gunya satisfeito, e com um sorriso partiu em direção ao Gunya de sua família, e lá dormiu, uma grande rede estava pendurada entre dois galhos, ele se aconchegou e então dormiu.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
E no dia seguinte, como Ngayhl previu, não apenas choveu, como a vegetação de Towurunga cresceu, e então ao decorrer das semanas, em 30 de janeiro, foi realizado um banquete, o conselho já vinha coletando larvas, raízes, frutas e carne para um banquete, e então fizeram disso para celebrar as chuvas e chegada dos "Sopros de Wonambi".
.
.
.
O assentamento tinha uma grande fogueira no centro, acendida por Dulbara, com lagartos assando à brasa junto de emus, wallabys e periquitos, gravetos com várias larvas fincadas e torradas também eram presentes juntos de vasos de frutas e raízes, para beber havia um poço próximo de água doce o qual Balunji coletava com baldes de madeira.
[i]Por fim os coalas não deram uma visão ruim, não é Ngarrajin?[/i]
Kyanga disse, enquanto ficava com seu cajado e totem do clã em suas costas segurando um copo cheio de suco de quandong, as roupas dele eram leves e mais como uma túnica que as vestes comuns, o deserto era mais frio a noite, por isso, Ngarrajin estava ao seu lado, segurando um graveto com pequenas larvas torradas, ele enfiou o palito por baixo de sua bandana e retirou logo em seguida, com algumas larvas a menos, com a voz abafada, ele olhou para Kyanga e disse.
[i]Enfim, boas notícias...[/i]
Logo em seguida veio Balunji, suas vestes eram longas mas finas, ele carregava um jarro com suco de quandong, e então os ofereceu, Kyanga aceito mais Ngarrajin não quis, Balunji com as mãos controlou o suco para ir até o copo de Kyanga.
[i]Sempre querendo se mostrar...[/i]
Ngarrajin murmurou para si mesmo.
Enquanto isso no centro, Ngayhl estava sentado, ele comia folhas de eucalipto, ao contrário dos outros que comiam oque tinha lá, Kaltimaka, do clã Penguji tomou um assento próximo do velho, ele usava vestes cerimoniais com penas de aves, em seu tórax podia ser visto, escondido em meio as penas, padrões espirais coloridos.
[i]Pq está comendo essas folhas, sábio, não são tóxicas?[/i]
O velho se virou para Kaltimaka e disse, seu tom calmo e suave.
[i]Eu não como só isso, mas o processo é simples, as menores são menos tóxicas, então deixe dois sóis para secar, e então estará pronta, nosso ancestral e irmãos coalas se adaptaram para alimentarem-se dessas folhas, nós precisamos de....etapas extras.[/i]
[i]Mas, pq isso?[/i]
[i]Essa é uma boa questão, conforme nos conectamos ao Dreamtime, podemos então não apenas evoluir em poder, como também em nível espiritual, é claro, esse é o meu método para me conectar com força ao Dreamtime...[/i]
O velho respondeu, com calma, Kaltimaka assentiu e então pegou um graveto com carne de lagarto, Ngayhl aceitou e disse.
[i]Mas não devemos entregar nossa vida apenas a isso, precisamos também focar em nosso corpo, mente forte e corpo forte, nosso corpo é o lar de nosso espírito, e, você certamente cuida bem de sua casa, não?[/i]
[i]Sim, obrigado pelo conhecimento.[/i]
Kaltimaka falou, agradecido pela sabedoria do coala sábio, conforme o banquete continuava, pessoas de todas idades iam perguntar algo para o sábio, que calmamente, respondia cada uma com a mesma sabedoria.
.
.
.
[i]Mardu? é você mesmo?[/i]
Balunji disse, surpreso ao ver o líder do clã Djarra presente no banquete, já que o mesmo preferia estar meditando profundamente à estar presente em celebrações.
[i]Eu não me tornei um espírito ainda, então creio que sim?[/i]
Ele riu em resposta, Balunji o ofereceu um pedaço de carne de lagarto, ele aceitou e devorou o pedaço em segundos.
[i]Clã da cacatua mas fome de um dingo hein?[/i]
Balunji brincou, e Mardu sorriu com a piada.
-
Tjilpi, Dulbara e Kialja estavam juntos discutindo qual tinha o melhor ancestral dentre os três.
[i]Claramente o periquito é superior, foi ele quem sacrificou suas penas e criou as nuvens que nos dão a chuva e a vida![/i]
Kialja exclamou , ela parecia orgulhosa de seu clã, deixando seu colar e capa de penas bem a mostra.
Dulbara então debateu de volta.
[i]E o Dingu sacrificou a si mesmo para nos dar o fogo, e é graças à essa chama que nós nos alimentamos e podemos substituir o mato velho pelo novo e trazer mais vida![/i]
Dulbara parecia igualmente orgulhoso sobre seu ancestral, ele usava um manto de pele de canguru sobre o corpo, mas não deixava de mostrar sua pintura corporal de dingu grande em seu peito com orgulho , na parte de baixo para se cobrir usava uma cinta com couro de canguru com espirais.
Tjilpi suspirou e então disse:
[i]Waadang(o ancestral corvo) foi quem ensinou nós humanos a falar, se não fosse por ele, nós estariamos catando paus e pedras e nem estaríamos falando disso[/i].
Foi então que Balunji apareceu e disse.
[i]Isso pode ser até verdade, mas Wonambi-[/i]
Os 3 cortaram Balunji respondendo em tom alto e severo.
[b] CALA BOCA NINGUÉM PEDIU SUA OPINIÃO [/b].
Balunji surpreso, recuou de volta e seguiu oferecendo comida e bebida para os presentes, enquanto o "trio" continuava debatendo.
-
[i]A maioria das pessoas descende de um clã apenas, e por consequência tem poderes limitados à apenas um clã, e eu? eu tenho 2, minha mãe descendia do clã Nynghna e meu pai de Dingu.
[/i]
Ngarrajin falou, com a voz abafada, contando para Tjarrampa.
[i]Mas pq?[/i]
O Líder do clã Canguru questionou.
[i]Pois meus pais eram de diferentes assentamentos que estavam em uma disputa que vinha ocorrendo por muito tempo, então o líder do assentamento Nynghna ofereceu a mão de sua filha, Merindah, para o filho do governante do outro assentamento, algo que meu avô detestou, mas aceitou, e então eu nasci, fruto da união de dois clãs.[/i]
Tjarrampa parece ter criado mais perguntas que respostas em sua cabeça.
[i]Mas e como você se tornou um mercador e andarilho.[/i]
Kyanga, que estava ao lado pergunta, Ngarrajin parece ter dado uma risada baixa.
[i] Pq eu livre, não quis os luxos de governar por sangue, mas queria conquistar por esforços, e outra, eu prefiro explorar o mundo À ter que ficar preso em um grupo por quase toda a vida por ser seu "sucessor".
[/i]
[i]Eh, justo.[/i]
Os dois responderem simultaneamente.
-
Após algum tempo depois de festividade e comida e bebida, começou-se a dança e canção.
[b]Ngurrugu Tjungu, a dança da abundância.[/b]
Ngayhl ficou com os tambores, junto de Balunji e Mardu, enquanto Kialja, Tjilpi , Wurtalpa e Kyanga sopravam os didgeridoos, várias pessoas se arrumaram em círculo de frente uma para a outra, em várias filas, e então posicionaram-se, com um joelho semi-flexionado atrás e outro um passo a frente, com as mãos de lado com a palma a mostra, conforme o ritmo dos tambores, eles davam um passo para frente e moviam os braços para cima e para baixo.
Então logo muda, as crianças, na primeira fileira(mais próxima da fogueira) saltitam e movem os braços de forma mais fluída e livre, os adultos nas segunda e terceira fileira gritam batendo as mãos na boca : 
[b]NGURRA NGURRA![/b]( O significado de Ngurra se perdeu no tempo, mas é um grito ritualístico milenar dos Alkiragunya).
Enquanto os mais velhos na última fileira andavam em zigue zague como serpentes com o corpo curvado e mãos coladas ao corpo.
[i][b]Ngaparrutu[/b], [b]Alkira[/b], [b]Tjumpi[/b][/i](Unidos, terra, sonho, isso é, unidos pela terra, e sonhos)
Os três guardiões gritaram uníssonos conforme também aceleravam o ritmo da batida, até que a batida cessa, os dançarinos se unem dando as mãos e as levantando para o alto e então os didgeridoos começaram a serem soprados, as fileiras de pessoas começam a rodar em torno da fogueira, e após 5 giros ,eles cessam, a dança propriamente dita termina, mas muitos apenas seguem dançando em pares, conforme a celebração se estende por toda noite.
-
[i]Eles realmente amam festejar.[/i]
Ngarrajin disse observando a dança ao redor da fogueira de uma rocha, apoiado em uma das pernas, ele olha para o lado e vê a figura de Tjarrampa ao seu lado, segurando um copo de suco de quandong, ele brinda com Ngarrajin .
[i]Sempre tão introvertido, mas ainda portador de grande inteligência e compreensão.[/i]
Tjarrampa falou para Ngarrajin tentando conversar, mas ele apenas olhou para Tjarrampa , embora escondido por sua bandana, ele sorriu.
[i]E sempre que não quer falar, responde sorrindo por trás desse tecido.[/i]
E assim continuaram pelo resto da noite...

----------------------

[b] January 12, 2024[/b]
When the 3 Guardians, Balunji, Mardu and Ngayhl meet together in a settlement, usually in Djamuturu (rainy season), many ask them for advice and revelations, that's what Tjarrampa, from the Marrapinti clan, went to ask Nghayhl about a dream, he wore thick brown clothes, he rolled up his own hair to distract himself while he went to the Koolemany gunya.
[i]Great sage, last night I had a strange dream.[/i]
He said as he entered and bowed, Ngayhl then looked at him, his eyes seemed focused not only on the visitor, but on his own soul.
[i]What did you dream.[/i]
He asked, already starting to hold the eucalyptus leaf around his neck. [i]I dreamed of dark, very dark clouds, which instead of rain fell spears of honey, the moment they reached a dry lake, it revived and filled with water and golden fish jumped out of it[/i].
The wise man smiled, and then relaxed his grip on the totem, and said to Tjarrampa.
[i]This is a sign of a prosperous feast and rains.[/i]
[i]Abundance? Excellent, I thank you.[/i]
Tjarrampa smiled in response and then left the Gunya satisfied, and with a smile he went towards his family's Gunya, and there he slept, a large hammock was hanging between two branches, he snuggled up and then slept. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
And the next day, as Ngayhl had predicted, not only did it rain, but the vegetation of Towurunga grew, and so as the weeks went by, on January 30th, a feast was held, the council had already been collecting grubs, roots, fruits and meat for a feast, and so they made it to celebrate the rains and the arrival of the "Breaths of Wonambi".
.
.
.
The settlement had a large bonfire in the center, lit by Dulbara, with lizards roasting on the coals along with emus, wallabys and parakeets, twigs with various grubs stuck in and roasted were also presented along with pots of fruits and roots, for drinking there was a nearby well of fresh water which Balunji collected with wooden buckets. [i]Finally the koalas didn't give a bad view, did they Ngarrajin?[/i]
Kyanga said, as he stood with his staff and clan totem on his back holding a glass full of quandong juice, his clothes were light and more like a tunic than common clothes, the desert was colder at night, so Ngarrajin was at his side, holding a twig with small roasted larvae, he stuck the stick under his bandana and pulled it out right away, with a few less larvae, with a muffled voice, he looked at Kyanga and said.
[i]Finally, good news...[/i]
Soon after came Balunji, his clothes were long but thin, he carried a jar with quandong juice, and then offered them, Kyanga accepted but Ngarrajin didn't want it, Balunji with his hands controlled the juice to go to Kyanga's glass.
[i]Always wanting to show off...[/i]
Ngarrajin muttered to himself.
Meanwhile, in the center, Ngayhl was sitting, he was eating eucalyptus leaves, unlike the others who ate whatever was there, Kaltimaka, from the Penguji clan, took a seat next to the old man, he wore ceremonial robes with bird feathers, on his chest could be seen, hidden among the feathers, colorful spiral patterns.
[i]Why are you eating these leaves, wise man, aren't they toxic?[/i]
The old man turned to Kaltimaka and said, his tone calm and soft. [i]I don't eat only this, but the process is simple, the smaller ones are less toxic, so leave them for two suns to dry, and then they will be ready, our ancestor and koala brothers adapted to feed on these leaves, we need... extra steps.[/i]
[i]But why is that?[/i]
[i]That's a good question, as we connect to the Dreamtime, we can then not only evolve in power, but also on a spiritual level, of course, this is my method to connect strongly to the Dreamtime...[/i]
The old man answered calmly, Kaltimaka nodded and then picked up a twig with lizard meat, Ngayhl accepted and said. [i]But we shouldn't just give our lives to that, we also need to focus on our body, a strong mind and a strong body, our body is the home of our spirit, and you certainly take good care of your home, don't you?[/i]
[i]Yes, thank you for the knowledge.[/i]
Kaltimaka spoke, grateful for the wisdom of the wise koala, as the banquet continued, people of all ages would ask the wise man something, who calmly answered each one with the same wisdom.
.
.
.
[i]Mardu? is that really you?[/i]
Balunji said, surprised to see the leader of the Djarra clan present at the banquet, since he preferred to be meditating deeply than to be present at celebrations.
[i]I haven't become a spirit yet, so I guess I have?[/i]
He laughed in response, Balunji offered him a piece of lizard meat, he accepted and devoured the piece in seconds. [i]Clan of the cockatoo but hungry as a dingo, huh?[/i]
Balunji joked, and Mardu smiled at the joke.
-
Tjilpi, Dulbara and Kialja They were discussing together which had the best ancestor among the three.
[i]Clearly the parakeet is superior, it was he who sacrificed his feathers and created the clouds that give us rain and life![/i]
Kialja exclaimed, she seemed proud of her clan, leaving her feathered collar and cape clearly visible.
Dulbara then argued back.
[i]And the Dingu sacrificed himself to give us fire, and it is thanks to this flame that we feed ourselves and can replace the old bush with new and bring more life![/i]
Dulbara seemed equally proud of his ancestor, he wore a kangaroo skin cloak over his body, but he did not fail to show off his large dingu body paint on his chest with pride, on the lower part to cover himself he wore a kangaroo leather belt with spirals. Tjilpi sighed and then said:
[i]Waadang (the crow ancestor) was the one who taught us humans to speak, if it weren't for him, we would be picking up sticks and stones and wouldn't even be talking about it[/i].
It was then that Balunji appeared and said.
[i]That may even be true, but Wonambi-[/i]
The 3 cut Balunji off, answering in a loud and severe tone.
[b] SHUT UP NOBODY ASKED FOR YOUR OPINION[/b].
Balunji, surprised, retreated back and continued offering food and drink to those present, while the "trio" continued to debate.
-
[i]Most people descend from just one clan, and consequently have powers limited to just one clan, and me? I have 2, my mother descended from the Nynghna clan and my father from Dingu.
[/i]
Ngarrajin spoke, with a muffled voice, telling Tjarrampa.
[i]But why?[/i]
The Kangaroo clan leader questioned.
[i]Because my parents were from different settlements that were in a dispute that had been going on for a long time, so the leader of the Nynghna settlement offered the hand of his daughter, Merindah, to the son of the ruler of the other settlement, something that my grandfather hated, but accepted, and so I was born, the fruit of the union of two clans.[/i]
Tjarrampa seems to have created more questions than answers in his head.
[i]But how did you become a merchant and wanderer.[/i]
Kyanga, who was next to him, asked, Ngarrajin seemed to have given a low laugh. [i] Because I am free, I did not want the luxuries of ruling by blood, but I wanted to conquer by effort, and besides, I prefer to explore the world than to have to stay stuck in a group for almost my entire life because I am its "successor".
[/i]
[i]Eh, fair enough.[/i]
The two answered simultaneously.
-
After some time of festivities and food and drink, the dancing and singing began. [b]Ngurrugu Tjungu, the dance of abundance.[/b]
Ngayhl stood with the drums, along with Balunji and Mardu, while Kialja, Tjilpi, Wurtalpa and Kyanga blew the didgeridoos. Several people lined up in a circle facing each other, in several rows, and then positioned themselves with one knee semi-bent behind and the other one step forward, with their hands at their sides with the palms showing. According to the rhythm of the drums, they took a step forward and moved their arms up and down.
Then it soon changed, the children, in the first row (closest to the bonfire) jumped and moved their arms more fluidly and freely, the adults in the second and third rows shouted, clapping their hands over their mouths:
[b]NGURRA NGURRA![/b] (The meaning of Ngurra has been lost in time, but it is an ancient ritual cry of the Alkiragunya). While the elders in the last row walked in a zigzag pattern like snakes with their bodies bent and their hands glued to their bodies.
[i][b]Ngaparrutu[/b], [b]Alkira[/b], [b]Tjumpi[/b][/i](United, land, dream, that is, united by the land, and dreams)
The three guardians shouted in unison as they also accelerated the rhythm of the beat, until the beat stopped, the dancers joined hands and raised them high and then the didgeridoos began to be blown, the rows of people began to spin around the bonfire, and after 5 spins, they stopped, the dance itself ended, but many just continued dancing in pairs, as the celebration continued throughout the night. -
[i]They really love to party.[/i]
Ngarrajin said watching the dance around the fire from a rock, leaning on one of his legs, he looks to the side and sees the figure of Tjarrampa next to him, holding a glass of quandong juice, he toasts with Ngarrajin.
[i]Always so introverted, but still carrying great intelligence and understanding.[/i]
Tjarrampa spoke to Ngarrajin trying to talk, but he just looked at Tjarrampa, although hidden by his bandana, he smiled.
[i]And whenever he doesn't want to talk, he responds smiling behind this fabric.[/i]
And so they continued for the rest of the night..

[b][u]The renewed push north and Irohgrad[/u][/b]

[spoiler=Expansion post 2. electric bogaloo][u][b]Aftermath of the eastern meeting[/b][/u]

After making contact with the Alkiragunya at the end of 955 AD, and having the first camels interoduced to Nordiheim, it was quickly understood that they would need more camels for the future as they proved incredebly good at traversing the lands that the Nordiheimians called home, as they did not have the same problems crossing larger distances were there was little to no water for long stretches of the journey, this meant that the large expanses of dry land and savanas came into their reach for the first time.

It was decided that a trade post would be built and maintained near the lands that was more or less understood to be the home of the Alkiragunya to invite further trade ,and if possible get more camels, this trade post would after a while be given the name of "Traders Point" and would be the place marking the most eastern land that the Nordiheimians had ever traveled to at this point in their entire history, someting that would not change for a very long time.
There was also given a directive to the traders of Nordiheim to seek out tribes, traders and communeties in the east that wasent the Alkiragunya but still had camels to gain more of them trough trade or deals so that they could obtain enough camels to breed them sustainably at home to meet the demand that would most certainly apear at home.

Tough at start of the year 957 AD many Nordiheimans, especialy Midlandians of the northern part of Nordiheim, felt that enough time and resources had been spent at eastern buisiness and it was time to focus on the north again, for there had been news from the exploration team that was sent there that they had heard tales about a settlement further north and that the people who lived there shared similarities with them.
These could joust be people that had traveled north in the past to get away from the nobles destructive rule, but they could also be from the group that had left thier ancestors 'Exodus' when they came to the shores of this continet, someting that could not be ignored.

However, the travel north was not done easely by the exploration team and had taken a long time, any further exploration up north would have the same problem at this time aswell, but if given some patience they could atain enough camels to use them to explore the land up north much faster then before.
This was seen as the smartest choice by the majorety of Nordiheimians.

[b][u]The renewed push north and a meeting with the people of irohgrad[/u][/b]

While it had taken a bit longer than it had been expected, by the year 960 AD Nordiheim had managed to aquire enough camels to afford to creat the first camel expedision team, made up of 12 people were 3 of them designated as the leaders (1 from each region), who was ready to travel north to find more information about the Easterners from the old tales of the Exodus and get in contact with the town of Irohgrad, perhaps even entice them to join Nordiheim as a new region.

The Vestland carpenters from the middle of Nordiheim had crafted sturdy yet light wagons for the camels to pull that could be filled with water and food for the journey incase waterholes was harder to find then expected, and the leather workers of Sorland in the south had created saddels for the camels inspired by the saddels used by the Alkiragunya that the eastern expedition had told about.
Equiped with all this, and the camels having drunk their fill from the small lake up by the city of Midgard, the expedition sett out towards the north from Nordiheim as the cold season was about to start in Argos, the people of Nordiheim would wait in anticipation of the news they would hopefully bring back in a year or two if noting went horribly wrong.

After decending the northern part of Red wall mountain, were the northern most part of Nordiheim was at this point in history, the expedition would enter the northern savana plains of Argos, tough it was dry and hot with tall yellow grass it still had a certain peace to it that was only interupted by the occasional animal that would observe the expedition at a safe distance, the sound of birds could be heard every now and then from the expance of the plains together with the ocasional kangaroo pack, the expedition even spooted a sizeable mob of emus in the distance.

Tough at one point the expedition got itself a bit of a scare as the spoter of the group made them aware that a large iron drake was coming towards them, and it seemed to come with focused intent, a midlandian in the group recogniced the iron drakes body language as it being on the hunt tough it seemed far more intense, as if it was in some kind of trance and haden't even noticed the humans of the group, it had its gaze squarely locked on the camels.
The eldest of the group, and a seasoned traveler, quickly made the decision to release one of the extra camels they had been given for the journey, to be used as a reserve, chasing it so it would run away from the group but close enough to the drake to draw its atention away from them.
This seemed to work as the iron drakes gaze almoust immidiatly went to the now lone camel who it quickly went after, the expedition group increased its pace to get extra distance between themself and the large drake that was now preoccupied, tough they could still hear it when the drake managed to catch up with it as the camel gave out a loud and pained grunts, the two members of the group that was at the rear claimed that they saw the large iron drake use a burst of terrifying speed to catch up with the camel and rip one of its hind legs off with its powerfull jaws before going for the trouth of the then cripeled camel, a rather disturbing memory to gain.

The rest of the journey was thankfully filled with far less encounters of iron drakes, only encountering a singel pair of earth drakes that backed off the moment the group made it obvious they had allready seen them, tough they did start to encounter small vandering groups of locals and even a small tribe that gave them bether direction towards Irohgrad, aswell as curious questions about the large and strange beasts they were riding.
With the helpfull directions from the locals the expedition group would finnaly reach the town of Irohgrad, a rather odd looking town, with a buildings built with a mixed architecture of what could be called the Aboriginal style and what was clearly some type of Nortiheimian style with norse dragon decorations at the ends of the roof beams.

The people of Irohgrad was also mixed, Aboriginals and people with various amount of mixed features from the Norse and Aboriginal peoples lived together with little issue, similar to how it was in Nordiheim but with the ratios being opposite, though they were a bit wary of them as strangers from the deep south they were non the less welcoming, as they agreed to let the 3 leaders of the group meet with their leader for talks.

[u][b]The meeting with the Leader of Irohgrad[/b][/u]

The three leaders of the expedition walked into the largest building in the town that they had been directed to, it was only one floor high for the most part, but had a high roof and a tower that was 4 stories tall in the middel of its structure that was adorned with many carvings of local animals on the roof and around the doors and windows with the dragon taking center stage everywere, tough at closer inspection they could now see that the dragons were actualy drakes, earth and iron drakes could be seen with there different crests, tough there was also another one that looked different from what they had ever seen and seemed to have been deliberatly made noticeable smaller then the two other types.

Tough they looked around at the decorative carvings of the building that continued inside, they did not let it delay them in proceeding into the main hall of the building that was placed under the tower they had seen from the outside, when they eneterd the main hall they were greeted by the elderly man that was the towns leader, but they also couldent help to see the 3 statues of drakes at the back of the room, in the center was the iron drake painted a very similar dark iron grey color that made it look almoust lifelike and a bit disturbing to the 3 men considering the meeting with one earlier in their journey, the one to the right was obviusly a earth drake carved expertly out of wood that had a similar brown color to the real ting, the last one however was of a drake that they had never seen before and had no record off, its was much smaller then the other two and was colored with some cind of material that made it look as green as fresh leafs, its crest was much smaller but its legs and toes were very long compared to its size and ended in wicked looking claws and its maw whas fille with small razor like teeth unlike the more powerfull and sturdy looking teeth of other drakes.

The elderly man invited them to sit by the table at the center of the room that had a mug with 4 cups made from red clay on it, when the 3 Nordiheimians had taken their seats at the table the man poored them each a drink from the mug, the drink had a opaque greenish hue to it, the man introduced himself as Chief Yarramundi.
Ones he himself was seated he asked the 3 what they came to Irohgrad for, to wich the three answered tough with the one from Vestland taking the lead being both the most open and honest with the chief letting no "high education" words sweeten the truth.
Tough at one point the odd smaller drake, wich the chief called a 'Tree Dragon' came up wich brought forth Irohgrads slightly unique relligion were both the dreamtime of the Aboriginals and the dragons of the Nordiheimian Asatru relligion seemed to have been mixed together, this quickly broght chief Yarramundi into a seemingly intense religious discusion with the Sorlandian of the group, this discusion lasted for a bit with the 2 other Nordiheimians getting woried were it would go yet being unsure how to intervene, tankfully the religious discusion seemed to end on a unspoken agreement that they were similar enough to accept each other as simply two different sides of the same truth, tough more discussion would proberly need to be had between priests.

With the religious part being ower the 2 other of the group could breath a sileng sigh of relief and ask were they could see this 'tree dragon' and what the juice they had been given to drink was made of as they had never tasted someting like it before.
Chief Yarramundi answered that both the 'tree dragon' and Kakadu plum, that the juice was made from, could be found in the jungels joust a bit further north of Irohgrad, it could actualy be seen from the buildings tower if they wanted to see for themself.
The 3 were a bit supriced by this, was the green jungel that their anccestors told of in the few remaining texts of the exodus realy that close?, they accepted the offer from the chief to see it from the top of the tower.

[b][u]A view and promises at the top of a tower[/u][/b]

From the top of the tower you could indeed see the jungel to the north, even tough some of it whas obscured by mist seeming to come from its large trees, the 3 Nordiheimians gazed with wonder at the distant green sea that was so unlike what they were used to.
Chief Yarramundi stod beside them and asked joust how interested they were in the jungel and the greate lake that was on the other side of it, and was it mostly for food?
The Midlandian told him that it was not joust to find more fertile land to gain more food or the sea to gain fish, but more importanlty to find the Easterners that they had lost all contact with many generations ago when they splitt away from the great exodus of their ancestors.

The chief noded and told them that the 'Easterners', as they had called them, was indeed in the north by the coast but gave them a warning, while the Nordiheimians had managed to cast off the chains of their own nobels and striped them of power the same could not be said of the people from the north, there was always someone who came to Irohgrad and the lands around it every decade or so and they always brought tales of their nobels who seemed to be infused with a greed that sounded almoust like a disease that brought poverty and suffering to the people they ruled over with a heavy golden fist, and if they intended to bring Irohgrad and its sorounding villages into the folds of Nordiheim, as he suspected that they wanted to do, then he would need not only binding promisses that they would be protected but also the physical proof of defences.

The 3 Nordiheimians were a bit supriced by this demand, they had suspected that the westerners might also have had nobles that would claim power among them long ago but from what the chief was saying it sounded like these nobles might be worse then what their own had been wich was cause for worry.
They told the chief that their council would most likely agree to create defences for them when they learned about the northern nobels and how they rule, tough they might want to send someone to verify that it is the truth.

The chief nooded, it was only fair that they be allowed to verify it for themself, they may all go home with the news that Irohgrad is willing to join Nordiheim if all their demands of defence and equal representation are met by their council, tough he also pointed out that they might want to take a small detour slightly westward as they traveled south again for there was a village there that they had managed to miss on their journey here called Ngura that might have someting they would find interesting.

[b][u]Journey home and informing the Council[/u][/b]

Having stayed a few days in Irohgrad to rest and gain some new suplies for their journey back home the group of 12 Nordiheimians explorers gave their goodbyes to the people there started their trek back home, while this time they would fortunatly not have a close encounter with a hungry iron drake they did heed the sugiestion from chief Yarramundi and had their route stray slightly to the west to see what was so special about the small village of Ngura that they apperently had missed.

After a few days of travel they did indeed encounter a village they had noot seen, and no wonder as the village was somewhat hiden from affar as it had been build into a part of the land that was lower then the rest, and in the middel there seemed to be a open pit mine containing a suspiciously familiar white rock.
They aproched the village and greeted the people keeping guard at its entrance  saying they were Nordiheimians from the far south that were on their way home from Irohgrad but had been told by chief Yarramundi that they should visit this village on their way back, the raised some eyebrows before one said that he would get their leader.

It did not take long for the leader of this village to come to them, he introduced himself as Balun of Ngura and asked if they wanted to see their mine, someting that gave the 3 leaders of the Nordiheimians the fealing that he knew exactly why chief Yarramundi had told them about this village.
Geting close to the open pit mine they could see that the rock here did indeed seem familiar, members of this village mined the white rock wearing wrapings on their feet, someting that was not commen among the Aboriginal people.

When they asked Balun what this rock was he simply asked them if they would like to give it a lick, someting that the Vestlandian gladly accepted and did joust so, having given one of the white rocks a lick he turned to his fellow Nordiheimians and told them that this was indeed rock salt as they all suspected.
They asked Balun how much salt he and his people tought was in this area and he told them that while this was the place they had chosen to mine for it they had tried digging other places in the sorounding land and had found more of the white rock several places indicating that there was a fair bit of it around here.

The group now understod why chief Yarramundi had sugested they come here on the way back, salt was someting Nordiheim did not have enough off and had to create a council controlled guild for to make sure it was fairly distributed among the people, with this potentialy large salt vein in the Irohgrad area it would make the council way more likely to agree with all of their demands.
Before they could even ask Balun told them that he would like to send with them a small gift of rock salt for them to bring home to show their people what value the Irohgrad region could bring to the future of Nordiheim, this supriced the Nordiheimians a bit but they agreed, the 3 leaders figured that Balun most likely had been told about them before they got here proberly by bird or someting similar.

One of their wagons had most of its contents transfered to the reserve camels and was filled with as much rock salt that is could safely carry before the expedition team continued their travel home after giving thanks to the village of Ngura and their leader Balun who also told them of a watering hole they could stop by on their way home.
The Nordiheimians could see no reason why they shouldent stop by it so that they could mark it as accuratly as possible on their map for when others in the future were to travel north.

The rest of the journey back home was rather uneventfull and they returned home to Nordiheim to quite the exited crowd in the capital of Midgard.
By the evening of the day they returned to the capitol the 3 leaders of the expidition stood before the council of Nordiheim and told them the long tale of their journey leaving no detail out,
The council was happy that Irohgrad seemed willing to join Nordiheim and extatic that the Easterners and the coast seemed to be closer that what they had feared, but the news that they were ruled by nobles that sounded like they were as bad or worse then what their own had been was not good news.
If this was true then they could understand why one of the demands of the people of Irohgrad was the construction of defences for them, the oldest of the council that had actualy fought in the Great Commoner Revolution War over 20 years ago exclaimed [i]"All further plans must move forward with the assumption that the storries we have been told about them is true untill such time that it is proven wrong or right!"[/i], pretty much the entire council agreed with this assesment.
Tough it also helped that it had been discovered that the village near Irohgrad named Ngura had a potentialy large deposit of rock salt, that alone would proberly pay for the defences that would have to be made in the area to satisfy the people of the region.

The next day the council decided that a convoy of diplomats and traders would be gathered, together with some engineers and cartographers, to travel to Irohgrad and make propper talk and get them into the fold of Nordiheim and find were it was best to make the defences, aswell as setting up a trade route for salt from the area.
There would also need to be sendt a secret scouting unit to gain more info about the nobles that ruled over the Easterners and how accurate the info about their rule was.

It was going to be some long years before they would be ready to make contact with them and it would end up being an odd chapter in Nordiheims history. [/spoiler]
